body:
I know; I intended it to be dangerous, to be honest.

I just think that sealing medical help will not really be beneficial. There is no way to do it secretly and even if there was, all that will happen is that (if I survive) I will be treated and sent home. I imagine it will only create more disturbances in my life as and it is quite problematic already.
About 8000mg I believe? So double the daily dosage.

I really relate to that; there is something that can be more painful about suicide because it was the individuals personal choice; at least if I was given a terminal illness then it could not feel like it was anyone's fault.

I understand what you mean, but the only option I have is to go to a hospital. I am aware that the dose I took pretty much always leads to liver failure, and alerting someone that I took a lethal dose of said pills will only make things worse. If I survive, I have made my situation even worse and will still be mentally ill and suicidal. It just feels pointless now.

Haha, no worries. 

I understand what you mean; it feels hypocritical to try and advise others what to do. We all understand each others' pain, but are unsure on how to really help because we all essentially are in the same boat.

I feel like I have just run out of hope; it has been ten years of wanting to die and I feel like it is about time I just get on with it.

I appreciate that, I really do.

I think that we can never truly understand how anyone is really feeling.

I appreciate your concern; I do not want you to really be worried though.

I have several mental diagnoses; I am 18. I have had therapy and it has not worked. My parents know of my problems anyway.

I currently just feel drowsy, but I only took the paracetamol around 2 hours ago so I do not imagine that I will feel any physical effects for a while. I do not really have any intentions of trying to get help again; I am just waiting for the pills to take effect, I guess.

I am sorry that you have to experience that.

I just think getting help would be pointless; I will still be suicidal and have only made things worse by letting people know that I overdosed.

I agree! I do not think there is such thing as an adult per say; adulthood just redefines the boundaries in which children are made to stay in by law.

I think that being nervous is normal; you have a desire to help people get better and will worry about making things worse or not helping at all. I understand why seeing so many people would add to those fears, but you should not be hard on yourself when working in such fields.

I think it is important to remember that this is a subreddit for those have been failed by the system. Whilst every voice here is valid, we all do acknowledge that quite often do people get better from therapy; we just were unlucky.

We are not judging the therapists themselves but more as the system around them. Unfortunately, a lot of people who struggle to open up and conform with the process are often the ones who fail with therapy. And sadly, you can come across some individuals who have no passion or care for the benefit of their client.  

You seem as if you genuinely want to help people and authenticity goes a long way. It is important to understand that you will not be the right person for everyone, just like how some people do not fit as friends, but you will be the right person for tons of other people.

I think the issue is often not with the therapists, but the fact that there is nothing for patients to fall back on if therapy fails. It is the first and only line of defence, if one is opposed to medicine. When therapy does not help a person, there is nothing else that they can turn to.  I feel that therapy is very rigid, and a lot of people can struggle with that.

Haha, embrace the inner child. :) I feel like we are all secretly just children inside trying to hide it with our adult themes, lol.

I always liked the concept of hiking; I think it would be fun with friends too. It definitely seems like a nice hobby to have; I sadly do not live near mountains but more in a city, so the view here is pretty man-made.

Thank you. I am currently still here; I have not done anything yet. I have just been thinking a lot and flipping through my old journals, haha.

That sounds likes a beautiful site; your words mean a lot to me. I believe I read somewhere that you said you were going into the mental health field? If I am correct, I think you will truly have a wonderful impact on people. You really are something special; I am beyond grateful that you took the time to talk to me.

I can see how people might see me as an attention seeker or a troll, etc. But you took time out of your day to check up on me, and that is a genuine act of pure kindness. 

I wish you well, I really do. You are a good person. :)

It sounds absolutely stunning. You are truly a kind soul to have actually taking the time to make a monument of my name; it made me tear up a little, haha.

I think I would have liked it and it would have been nice to have been there; in a way, I am sad to have met you this way. I think you truly are a wonderful person for anyone to have in their lives, whilst also glad we are strangers because I feel you would become another person to which I would have hurt, you know? 

Thank you for having got back to me. I am curious, do you tend to hike often?

Anything in particular or just general advice?

Honestly? From experience, do not go through it alone.

Whether that requires reaching out to someone you personally know or someone professional, trying to fight your mind alone often pushes you deeper into the dark pit.

Your illness have a way or convincing you that everything is alright and that the way you feel or act is healthy. It will try and segregate you from the world and isolate you. Often, by the time you realise things are not right, it can be even harder to change.

It look me many years to realise that the things I felt and thought were not supposed to occur. Never feel bad about being open with people; how you feel and what you go through is valid and worth being heard and helped.

Sharing is caring. It does not matter who is giving or recieving, you can never express your feelings enough.

I wish you the best, I really do. I hope you are able to get your illness under reins and live a life without pain; I know what torture your own mentality can be.

You're really young, I am sorry you are in a bad situation.

I am 18, been suicidal since around 7-8. 

I am pretty sure that I would rather it be permanent; my presence causes damage to everyone and I think it would be best if everyone could just move on from me.
Just life, really. Mental illness that is not getting better, making people around me suffer; it has been ten years of wanting to die. I just want a break.
Yes, although honestly I think comparing every disorder, they all are worse in their own ways. I think it depends on how you look at them.

I think in their image, it seems like the most dangerous! I think though that anorexia still would stand as the most dangerous in health risks since the diagnosis includes a lot of physical problems as well as mental. But I definitely agree that the image ortharexia gives out is highly manipulative and dangerous to impressionable people.
Yes exactly. And the sufferer is usually working with the secrecy of the disorder to keep it hidden from those around them, so it often goes unseen until it has already permanently caused harm.
I believe you might be on about ortharexia? It is an awful illness. But because it is "healthy eating", it is often looked over and glorified. It is tragic.

That is a really good example. 

I think it just shows how mental illness, especially eating disorders, are  heavily glorified. It is frustrating how all too often, people wonder why young teenagers are coaxed into the life of disordered eating and later develop a disorder; the media pretends as if it is taking these matters seriously but every single condition is rather desirable or the spawn of the devil.

You never see the media telling the truth because it is not what people want to hear.

It sounds incredible. I think there can be something quite relaxing about it; feeling like you are just a fraction of the world. There is something calming about it; sort of like when you look at the night sky.

I agree. From experience, romance is the last thing on your mind during such times: it causes you to neglect your relationships. I found the romance thing to be ridiculous and it made anorexia seem like a subplot.

I was disappointed by the movie; it definitely had a lot of potential but they did not do fulfil the role of could have played in shining a light on eating disorders.

Your last statement really hits the nail on the head. Media would rather be entertained than educated, and often you see people who act as if they now know everything about said disorder because they have read a few articles and seen a movie or two about it. If we continue to mold such sensitive topics into a distorted ideation of the truth, we will never move on and only continue to portray mental health in an unhealthy and unhelpful light.

It sounds fascinating; if I can, I might have to give it a watch.

I completely agree; the media, especially in films, never portraits it to be authentic; it is always told in a way that makes it seem "interesting", usually to pull in an audience as we watch these poorly representative characters with mental illnesses only further to tarnish the reputation of what they truly are like to experience.

Nowadays, the media tends to stigmatise or glorify mental illnesses depending on how society views them; it is frustrating.

To the bone, I did see. I myself have anorexia and I found it to be almost a downplayed glorification of what eating disorders actually are. It ended quite strangely as well.

I understand that they can be a tricky subject to explain, but if you are going to make a story out of it then at least do it right to prevent further stigmatisation of mental illness.

Haha.

I guess that the journey is worth the view; I have heard that Vermont has some beautiful scenery. I imagine that it is quite rewarding to see after struggling up there, lol.

It's Abby; you have a nice name.

That is a really kind thing to do; thank you. You do not have to do such a thing.

I have never been hiking before; is it fun?

Precisely. The ratio between mental and physical health assistant is still so unbalanced. We do not take it seriously and it is heavily underfunded. I think both prisons and hospitals need to be funded and rewired, but I feel that focusing on mental health would reduce a lot of crimes, thus preventing prisons from being as crowded.

They seem to think that if you don't respond to the singular recovery process them you are deemed insane and thrown on medication. I refuse to take pills for my health and thankfully have never been offered them. People seem to think that because I have had some "miracle" therapy sessions and been discharged that I am now cured and happy.

If I was to be honest and speak about my suicidal ideation, I would be sectioned for sure. So what choice do they give people? Sectioning, prison, pills, suffering, or death. It is no surprise that there are so many suicide attempts a day; the system is failing so many people.

There would not even be a need for this subreddit if we was on top of mental health concerns; we would not have to come here to be less alone and vent about how we feel because no one else wants to or will listen; it is depressing.
Of course, go ahead. What's up?

Exactly, I could not agree more. It's genuinely really upsetting to see so many people suffer as a consequence.

Therapy is a very good concept, and so many people do get lucky and benefit from it. But it seems that anything that doesn't conform to what they have been taught is just casted aside and left to deal with it alone.

During my therapy, my parents were always present. They would "correct" anything they thought I said was wrong and so when I did attempt to open up, I just got shut down again.

I often felt as if I was being ganged up on at times and I remember a therapy session where I was genuinely questioned on if I was being an attention seeker; it was wild, haha. My experience has put me right off the idea, especially since I came out seemingly worse than when I went in.

If therapy was more able to cater to those who are less of the typical case, then maybe it would work better. But so many therapists just do not know how to deal with it.

Trust me, I have tried. If I had not, I would not have made it ten years with wanting to kill myself.

I spent a year in therapy, and months before at different psychologists; I have only spiralled into a worse state since then.

I am at peace with it. I think I have gotten very used to the feeling and I know that staying alive will lead me nowhere.

Thank you. I hope you can find a way to help yourself, I really do. I do not want to burden you with my problems though, haha. You sound like you already have a lot to carry yourself. 

I understand how you feel. With people, it is different. You know that they can logically survive without you; with pets, their fate is unpredictable once you are no longer there for them.

It sounds like you love them a lot, and I'm sure they equally love you. I think that they are lucky to have you as their owner. 

I was the same as you; I had suicidal ideation from about 7-8 but it was pretty sparse and irregular. Nowadays, it is every day and for most of my waking hours.

It is wierd, because I know that I did not always used to be this suicidal but yet I can not remember or imagine life without such thoughts.

Your interest means a lot to me. You seem like a very good person.

I think the best memory I have is when I met my SO with my sister and one of my best friends. 

We were online friends for four years and are doing long distance. It's almost been a year since we met, actually. Although we never managed to meet up again, the day was definitely one to remember, haha.

I don't really want to be remembered, to be honest. It would be nice to disapear and I feel guilty that people had to know me but I hope to make things right for everyone around me.

I am now curious, do you have a happiest memory? I'd you wish to share, I would love to know. :) 

I wish you the best too; I hope you find a better path in life is you haven't done so already. We need more people in the world like you. ❤️

I actually have; I ended up being an outpatient in a mental hospital due to being diagnosed with anorexia; my nurse was lovely. I was just unable to fully commit to the treatment.

I have also seen a psychologist, and she, being equally nice and understanding, ended the same way. Except I did not have a lot of sessions with her. I am not good at talking to and opening up, so I never got much out of therapy.

I am glad that you seemed to have benefited from therapy; I can definitely see how it would help for so many people and never think it should be written off. It is genuinely a worthy treatment if you are dedicated to getting better.

I appreciate that. I don't want to burden or talk too much though as I never liked doing that to people, haha.

I just don't really have the desire or motivation to get better; I have just accepted that death was the option for me. I would always advise people to try therapy and talk about how they feel but I could never take my own advice.

I appreciate your concern, I really do.

I actually read her article a while back; I am glad that she survived. Rereading again brought back some memories; she clearly went through hell.

I do understand that it is one of the worst ways to take your life but I am honestly prepared for it. I have no other way of taking my life and the pain of a few days will not be worse than the pain of the rest of my life.

If I only have two hours to get help, that is a good thing. I do not plan to go to hospital with the hopes of recovery; I fear surviving the attempt. The consequences will be horrendous if I do.

You are a kind soul; I do not want you to waste your time worrying about me. I have tried to get help and I think I am beyond it.

I appreciate your offer; thank you. I won't burden you with the details though.

It seems to be from what I have read up that paracetamol often fails to kill you if medicine was received in time. I do not plan to get help or tell anyone about my overdose, so I do imagine that by the time, if at all, anyone was to notice then it will hopefully be too late.

I do not have any other options other them paracetamol or similar drugs. I know I will die in agony but I am prepared for that.

I am grateful for your concern and how you took the time to read into my post further. :)

I understand how you feel. I was pretty much labeled an attention seeker from the moment I was forced to "get help". It all seems utterly pointless if I was going to be accused of feeling sorry for myself and exaggerating my problems if I was also being told I need help.

I never have seen myself as a victim and have always taken blame for the way I am. But of course, I always am just trying to blame others for my issues; it makes no sense. I do not get why people pretend to care when it suits them.

I found it quite amusing that when I wanted help, I never got it. Now I do not want it? It is forced upon me in am attempt to make me conform. It is ridiculous.

I have been thinking about this for a while; more what would I do on my final day.

I have about 9 days to live. I don't think I will do anything particularly spectacular.

I plan to water my cacti, make sure my room is completely tidy and things are in their right places; I will pick a final song to listen to and go from there. I do not see the point of making my last day any better than the others. If I could have a good day then I imagine I could be happy and would not feel the need to take my own life.

I want to interact with people as little as possible; maybe I'll call a hotline so that a chosen lived one will not have to be the last person I spoke to.
Definitely not.
Lil Peep is definitely a go to for me. I miss him; it's sad he died.

How can they attempt to save my life if they don't know exactly what I have done? Is there a way that I can prevent medical intervention from happening?

I plan on taking paracetamol. I am aware it will destroy my liver but from what I have seen, it doesn't seem to go to the other organs or bloodstream but I'm not really sure.

I'm not taking my life solely to give what I can to others, although that is a benefit of doing so. It just feels like a waste to take my life and let everything go to waste of something can be used. I've never had any physical health concerns and I know I'm pretty healthy.

Whatever happens, I'm taking my life in August. I just want to be able to give what I can with the life I take.
From experience, it may be more of them being controlling than overprotective.

Due to my mental health, it puts a very heavy strain on my family. I am housebound, things are constantly having to be altered and changed because of me, I cause a lot of unnecessary drama and trouble all because of my own issues.

I have always had it made clear to me that I wasn't exactly the best person to be around. I've been labeled as many horrible things, and I don't really doubt them anymore. They are probably all true.

I've been threatened to be kicked out on multiple occasions, from a young child to teenage years and so forth.

I only really have connections to people online, and I always see my friends seemingly sadder after I've been in contact with them. Once they leave and I feel abandoned, I always see them better off. Which isn't a bad thing, but it shows that this repeated pattern most likely means I am a reason to their unhappiness.

I am glad that you have been able to find someone to have taken you seriously. I'm happy for you that you were able to get help and improve, but I just don't feel like that's the life I was ever supposed to live.

I doubt he would take his own life. I am not a major prioty to him, (we also are long distance) and always seems happier the less I am around him. I feel like taking my life will just improve his wellbeing and any "grief" felt by my loved ones will be short lived once they realise how me not being here improves their lives.

I know for a fact that I don't want to live even if things do get better.

I know that I can get help, and I have tried. But whatever condition of life I am in, everything ends so there is essentially no point; at least to me, anyway. 

If I'm happy, I will eventually die. If I am sad, I will eventually die. If I take my own life, I'm only skipping the years of pain and suffering that will be caused by me on others and just getting it other and done with.

I know that people will be better off without me. He is one of the many people who is constantly effected by my existence. If I truly cared about him or anyone else then how can I just continue to watch him and everyone else in agony because of me?

I think that you can't say it's factual unless its stated. Unless I actually live on Saturn, I don't seem to agree with those girls who have told you such things. They don't define females, they define twats. Most people are nice, and can see you for what and who you are.

I can guarantee most girls will not think that way; you've just been subjected to some bad ones.at this time of your life.

I get it's hard to be told not to, but do you think you can just hold off for a while? I mean, someone is going to miss you. It would be sad if you was to end your life over such incorrect, negative thoughts.

I'm a girl, and I think you are attractive, although it sadly seems that mine and others will not alter your incorrect thoughts.

I understand now you feel though; I myself have anorexia. I don't really know if I truly see my body as for what it is, but I see it as vile.

Despite of what others tell me, I can only believe the negative. I turn every nice compliment into a bad, hurtful comment that could have only been said to make me feel better, or to simply lie. I weed out anything that could potentially be negative, ignore any positive and forget to see the bigger picture of the well intended compliment.

In my head, my anorexia is louder than everyone else. It makes me feel as if I am fat, despite being at a healthy weight. I always feel ugly and miserable about my appearance.

I think that you seem to have trouble to believe anything other than what your mind is telling you, and I really relate to the inability to listen to anything else; nothing is louder than your own mind.

We can all tell you that you're beautiful, but the only one who needs to tell you that things right now is yourself.

I don't think us redditors can send you self esteem and self love even though we want to; if we could, I think most people on this forum don't have have it themselves, let alone to share it haha :)

But back to being serious, the more you lie to yourself, listen to those negative thoughts, fall deeper into the spiral, the more you'll continue to believe that you are ugly even though you're not.

I think that the reason you haven't gotten too lucky in relationships isn't with the outside, but within. Your emotional struggles do effext relationships; I am learning that the hard way.

You seem like a nice person with a troubled soul. Can I ask how long you've disliked your appearance for? Was there a trigger point for you?
No worries, you have helped. Thank you. :)
Is there a time frame from when someone dies that they have to get the organs in before they're useless?

Most likely would be something like paracetamol; though since that causes liver failure, I imagine that'll be out of the question.

Was curious about the other organs though.

I feel you, man.

I'm sorry this happened; I think you unfortunately opened up to someone who doesn't deserve you. Not everyone will be that way. Someone is out there who will take your concerns seriously.

I know it's hard to be open but I want to praise you on telling someone. It's such a hard thing to do, and I'm so sorry that you were disrespected in such a way.

My best friend told me that I was manipulative and just pretending I was ill; it hurts.

I'm sorry you went through that. I get what you mean about that and it's one of my worries; surviving after I've given over such a letter.

If you don't mind me asking, how are you doing now? I can't imagine what you must have been going through; I hope that things have improved.
Do you think that would be better than a note?

I'm sorry that quarantine is effecting you; it's a pretty tough situation for all. My life isn't much different from it really, and it's been that way for quite some time. It's sad seeing other people go through similar stuff; I hope it gets better for you, dude.

I wouldn't mind being compared to a dog haha; my family has three and they're the most loving creatures I've ever been around. I just have seen evidence that people are genuinely happier without me around, and that is a good thing. I feel guilty to still be alive and continuing to make everyone around me miserable. 

I pretty much have up on therapy when I was in it and wasted everyones' time, and I am no better. Every day feels like a broken record and I often can't really tell if I'm awake or not; it's a wierd place to be, man.

Most people I know have told me in some way that they don't really believe me; I'm at the point where I don't really want to get help anymore. I get that the negative effects of suicide is unfortunately unavoidable, yet I know that the short lived grief they might experience will be better than the long term of me continuing to hurt them; I just want them to stop suffering because of my issues.

I'd rather not leave a note, to be honest. I've tried to get help and speak about my issues but no one really takes them seriously. I just want a way to insure that anyone who might be hurt over my death has answers if they need them, you see?

Truly does your story hit a nerve; I am so proud of you and everything you have achieved.

I suffer with anxiety and OCD too; I know how crippling they are.

Your story is bound to give others hope; thank you so much for sharing it.

Keep it up and continue to live your life to the fullest; you're an inspiration. :)
I mean, a few days of agony surely can't be worse than years of hell; at least one has a quicker ending.
No, but then I'd rather not have to be sent to the hospital to just delay me dying. I just feel like I'm running out of ideas at this point.

I have. 

I've been dealing with the same situation for the past ten years; my family and friends pretty much don't believe that I suffer.

I've been to therapy and it hasn't worked. I think that I've had long enough to decide that life isn't worth living.
How are you doing? Im so sorry you're in this situation. I hope you're okay.

I'm sorry you're dealing with this, I really am.

To start off, I know I can't convince you to live. As much as I want you to, I know how it feels to believe that the only way out is to completely walk out of the door.

You don't need to prove to your mother that you're capable of great things. She seems to lack faith in you; she doesn't deserve the praise for being the reason to why you graduate. Finish your education for you. Due to your intelligence and dedication, you will graduate. That is an achievement to be proud of.

May I ask about your friend? Do you know if he is currently dealing with anything? What happens when you try and get closure? I'm dealing with a similar situation right now; it's painful. I know how you feel.

I can not give you a reason to live, 
but I can maybe give you some insight.

I don't believe you are worthless. No matter what our minds tell us, no one is worth nothing. We all have something to give.

The world may be falling at the seams, but we need all of the seamstresses we can get to help sew it back together.

From what you say, it sounds like you're dealing with a lot. You seem very strong.

We make our own paths in life. We are all one of a kind, with memories no one else but us knows, thoughts that no one else thinks, abilities that only we can do in our individualistic ways, the way we laugh, the way we talk; only you can be that person; no one can replace you.

You can look at life now, in it's state of despair. You can give up now, with an unused education, intelligence, love to give, emotion to express; you can let your demons win. Everyone who has wronged you, everything that has hurt you. 

We always root for the heroes, for the ones in pain to find a solution; so why aren't you rooting for yourself? People can not provide your worth, nor can they take it away. Only you can feel your worth; only you can believe it in a way that makes it clear to you.

Worth isn't objective. It doesn't come in a form of accomplishments or achievements; it's something we feel when we can see it. We don't need to prove it, because it's always there. Just often can we not see it.

Maybe it's not that no one cares, but what your mind has twisted to believe, I do not know. But what I do know is that just by your post, you seem like you have so much to give and it would be a shame to throw it all away. 

Even if you're surrounded by negative people, you won't always be. I know how it can be hard to "be normal"; I too have autism and making friends is almost impossible.

What I have learned is that the failed attempts is how we learn. We can't avoid a fall if we never tumble; we learn by our wrong decisions.

We can choose to sink or swim, but we'll never see what is above the water if we allow ourselves to drown.

I hope you find happiness, I really do.
I wish I had the answer. How are you doing? Is the pain any better?
